title: Flapjacks
subtitle: Chewy oat bars with golden syrup and butter
excerpt: Rolled oats bound with butter, golden syrup, and soft brown sugar, pressed into a tin and baked until golden. Chewy in the middle, slightly crisp at the edges. A British baking classic.

recipe.sourceNotes: The British flapjack is a baked oat bar made with golden syrup, butter, and sugar. It is completely different from the American pancake that shares the same name. The first British recipe appeared in 1935 in a Yorkshire cookbook. The texture depends on the ratio of syrup to sugar and the baking time: more syrup and a shorter bake gives a chewier result; more sugar and a longer bake gives a crisper one. Cut while warm, as they harden quickly on cooling.

content.text: Press the oat mixture firmly into the tin: any loose areas will crumble when cut. Watch carefully towards the end of baking as the edges catch quickly. Cut into bars while still warm, then leave to cool completely in the tin before removing: they firm up significantly as they cool.
Heat the oven to 170 C / fan 150 C / gas 3. Grease and line a 20 x 20 cm tin.
Melt the butter, golden syrup, and sugar together in a saucepan over low heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Remove from the heat.
Stir in the oats and salt until fully coated. Tip into the prepared tin. Press down firmly and evenly with the back of a spoon.

Bake for 22 to 25 minutes until golden all over. The centre will look slightly soft but firms up on cooling. Leave in the tin for 5 minutes, then mark into 16 bars with a knife. Leave to cool completely in the tin before removing.
